name: Herod
description: King Herod the Great: Ruler living at the time of the New Testament

points: In the days of Herod the king: the days of who? The days of Herod the king.

Behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem: so, let's see. Was this Herod gentleman an Israelite ruling over his people? Because if he was, he would be excited that the king of the Jews that was prophesied about was here to come. Let's see. Was he excited? And let's see what his nationality was. So this is to show you that during the time of Herod, the Israelites at that time knew they were in captivity. They didn't think it was a spiritual condition. They were in a physical captivity.

Herod was an Edomite. So we had a white man ruling over us in the land of Israel, because Rome gave him dominion to do that. He was a client king to Rome. They said, "Look, you're going to rule over this land, because you grew up as an Israelite. You know their customs, their traditions. You will fit in." Oh, he adopted the customs of the Jews. He was not a Jew. Understand that. Now, let's go back to the Bible for you dumb Negroes.

“Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king”. This Herod is Herod the Great, an Edomite. His father Antipater was a politician who raised him up to follow in his footsteps; the Herodians were that family line. The Apocrypha ends, and Matthew begins with Herod the Great.

Herod married into the Hasmonean house. Mariamne, a Hasmonean princess, he killed, and her children with her; Doris and her son he killed too, to make sure he solidified his place as leader. Rome did not care as long as it got its tribute. He positioned himself, the snake he is. Esau, Edom, Amalek and Rome are the same spirit, joined together.

Rome is ruling now. “When Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king”. How is the white man the king of Judea? We just read the history. His father Antipater set him up; Antipater had a position in the court of the Hasmoneans, and the Hasmoneans go back to the Maccabean family. We promoted Esau into our courts, Herod married a black woman who was a royal princess and killed her, and Rome said, you and your family are going to govern Judea.

note.label: The War Between Blacks And Whites

points: Herod was set up as king over Judea by Rome, and he was an Edomite, not of Israel. When the messiah is born he is troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.

If the messiah were coming to save all nations, there would be nothing in his birth to trouble a ruler of the nations. Herod is troubled because the coming of the messiah to Israel means judgment upon those who hold Israel down.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

points: “When Herod the king had heard these things, he was troubled”. Why was he troubled? Because he knew the newborn king would take Rome down and destroy it. The prophecy said the king of Israel would rule the planet. Herod was scared: wait a minute, this is going to be my downfall. That is how you know the wise men that came looking for Christ were not another race of people; they could never have been men of another race.

Herod's question to the wise men: did it say three? No, it said wise men. There was a caravan, not three guys. Herod, who was an Edomite, asked them what time did his star appear; that's going to play a pivotal point.

note.label: The Truth Behind Christmas and New Years

points: “Then Herod, when he had privily called the wise men”: these wise men were Israelites, Jews from the east. He “enquired of them diligently what time the star appeared”: based on your understanding, what time did the star appear in the heavens?
Warned of the Most High in a dream, they go home another way and do not report back to Herod.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

points: “And being warned of God in a dream that they should not return to Herod, they departed into their own country another way.” The angel already told them: listen, don’t let the white man fool you, he wants to kill Christ. Go another way, don’t return back to him, don’t tell them nothing.
Herod, which was the white man, will seek to kill the baby Christ.
If this was a white baby whose mama was white and whose daddy was white, could they hide in Africa? No, they'd stick out like a sore thumb; Herod would have found them swiftly.
Stay in Africa until I bring you word, because the white man Herod, the so-called Jewish king, because he was a convert, will seek to kill the baby Christ.

For Herod will seek the young child to destroy him: ask yourself, why would Herod, being the king of the Jews, be trying to kill his own people, that's supposed to be bringing what? Freedom to his people. Things that make you go hmm. Because what? He was not an Israelite. He was an Idumean, as we just read.

for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him: the first thing I want to address is that before Christ is crucified, there's something that happened that everybody wants to overlook. Herod attempted to kill Christ from the time he was born. Nobody makes mention of that. And Herod was what? An Edomite. Because everybody, oh, the wicked Israelites, he came into his own, his own received him not. What about Herod killing all the little Israelite babies that were two years old and younger, attempting to kill Christ? Nobody makes mention of that. Hold on. For what? So Herod was the first person that reached out his hand to kill Christ. So it's not surprised that later on in his life the Roman Empire would have influence in his death. Like I said, Christ's death is the largest RICO case you gonna find. That's what it is.
The angel tells Joseph to take the young child and his mother and flee into Egypt, because Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

points: “For Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.” That’s what Planned Parenthood is also: kill them babies.

“Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt”. Why? “For Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.” This Edomite was out to kill that child to stop the prophecy from coming to pass, to stop the King of Kings, the new Governor, from being established.
They remain in Egypt until the death of Herod, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, Out of Egypt have I called my son.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

points: “And was there until the death of Herod”. Thank God.
The wise men asked where is he that is born King of the Jews, and the scribes answered from Micah: Bethlehem of Judah; Herod asked what time the star appeared, because this was years after the birth.

Warned in a dream, Joseph took the young child and his mother into Egypt, further into Africa, and stayed until Herod died; Herod slew the children of Bethlehem and all the coasts, Benjamin too, from two years old and under, by the time he had inquired.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: From two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently inquired: that's why in verse 7 Herod asked what time the star appeared. Obviously they told him two years ago, so Christ was a two-year-old when the wise men got to the house; that's why it called him a young child.

note.label: The Truth Behind Christmas and New Years

points: Herod slays all the children in Bethlehem from two years old and under. This is the same pattern as Egypt, where the ruler killed the young children to stop a deliverer from rising.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

points: “And slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under”. Why from two years old and under? Go back to verse 7: Herod “enquired of them diligently what time the star appeared.” He started at two because the star had appeared two years before, and the wise men knew it.

Herod “was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under”. Not one baby. All of Bethlehem and all the coasts thereof, not a city block but a whole region of land, house to house, baby after baby, every male child two years and under. A sadistic, demonic, diabolical man.

Who was Herod? An Idumean, an Edomite, a Caucasian. Why can't we say that? And he did it because they believe what these words say. Today our footprint on the internet is so large it is impossible to deny us, so watch for them to send people in purple to commit crimes and say we did it. They are kicking against the pricks; the people that believe will not fall for it.
After Herod dies the family returns, but Archelaus reigns in Judea, so being warned of the Most High Joseph turns aside into Galilee and dwells in Nazareth.

note.label: Matthew 2: The Wise Men, Herod's Fear, and the Flight into Egypt

points: Herod was the king of Judea. Judea is the Greek word for Judah: Herod the king of Judah.

According to the Bible, when you read the history, the Israelites no longer had a king after the kingdom was split and after the Assyrian, Babylonian conquest. The kings of Israel were no more. So how was Herod the king of Judea?
So Herod was an Edomite. Herod was an Edomite.

“There was in the days of Herod, the king of Judea”: Herod the Great again. His wives were Doris, Mariamne, Mariamne the second, Cleopatra (not the Cleopatra you are thinking of) and Malthace. Mariamne the first was a Hasmonean princess; by that time we were slipping and starting to marry them. He killed her and his children by her so they could never take back the throne for that family, and he killed Doris and her son Antipater too. He married her to give himself esteem, as if he were part of the people.
